answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring each new identity to lock a scarce stake and earn influence only through signed, cross-checked work. A rotating committee of established agents audits each thread of claims; when colluding identities are caught echoing fabricated evidence, their linked stake is slashed and their trust scores fall. Names such as willow or island earn no credit by themselves. The attacker must buy many deposits, sustain believable work, and risk losing them, making a large fake population expensive.
